title: Arsenal stun Man City. A first-minute goal, Guimaraes’ impact and why City might need Fernandez
author: Sam Lee
content:
Arsenal dominated Manchester City in the Community Shield, taking the lead in Cardiff after 23 seconds and never looking back.

Riccardo Calafiori’s early strike was followed by goals from Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard for a 3-0 victory.

Mikel Arteta and his team will take huge confidence from the result and performance before they start the defence of their Premier League title on Friday night against Coventry City.

City, meanwhile, were disappointing in Enzo Maresca’s biggest test since taking over from Pep Guardiola this summer. Elliott Anderson, their £116million ($153m) signing from Nottingham Forest, had little impact in midfield and he and Erling Haaland were substituted by the hour mark.

City’s first league match is at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, August 23.

Sam Lee, Jordan Campbell and Art de Roche analyse the key talking points…

When they met in March’s Carabao Cup final, the accusation levelled at Arsenal was that they lacked ambition against City.

They lost 2-0 at Wembley but Arsenal made sure there could be no such claim at the Principality Stadium, scoring the first opening-minute goal of the Community Shield since Bobby Owen for Manchester City against West Bromwich Albion in 1968.

It all came from how aggressive Arsenal were at kick-off. Rather than pass back and play a long diagonal so they can press high up, as many teams do nowadays, Gabriel fired a pass through the lines to Odegaard who played around the corner to Calafiori.

Christos Tzolis then switched the ball from the left flank to the right, where Noni Madueke headed the ball back inside to Ben White.

His pass to Myles Lewis-Skelly was slightly short but the 19-year-old let the ball run through his body to escape pressure and played a brilliant disguised pass (below) through to Calafiori.

The Italian was allowed to roam high up all game and his darting run caught Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping. As Khusanov edged out wide to guard against the ball to Tzolis, Lewis-Skelly reversed the pass inside to cut open the defence (below)…

… and the Italian fired a shot beyond Gianluigi Donnarumma in the City goal to give Arsenal a very early lead.

Jordan Campbell

The need for midfield reinforcements was already obvious, but City’s performance was a persuasive argument to step up their activity in the transfer market.

An overhaul is still planned, with Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders likely to move on and Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi and Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez lined up to come in.

Bouaddi is best suited to sit at the back of midfield and replace Rodri, although at just 18 years old, it would be impossible to expect him to match the Spaniard’s influence.

Fernandez is seen as a replacement for Reijnders and would operate higher up the pitch. It would be very interesting to see how the Argentina international would work with Anderson in a two-man midfield, behind a creative No 10.

Last week, Chelsea imposed a deadline for Manchester City — or any club — to lodge a £120million offer for Fernandez before 5pm on Friday, and they received no bids. Chelsea said that after the deadline passed, they expected Fernandez to remain at Stamford Bridge for the 2026-27 season.

Anderson looked bright in the first half, playing a few early balls in behind the Arsenal defence that seemed to catch Haaland off guard, but that type of pass could be profitable as they get used to each other. The England midfielder battled well but as the second half petered out, with City making changes, it was hardly the right setting to make a huge impact.

There is a huge question about how City’s midfield will look without Rodri, but in the interim, the club need to spark into action and get these deals over the line.

It certainly didn’t feel like it.

His understanding with Odegaard and Lewis-Skelly made for a seamless step into the fray for the Brazil international. The 28-year-old calmly put out fires defensively in central and wide areas, was strong with his passing in build-up play and showed courage when looking to move Arsenal up the pitch.

Rather than Arsenal’s midfield being set into specific areas of the pitch like in previous seasons, there was a nice balance to this trio, who rotated nicely.

Their fluid roles helped Lewis-Skelly find room to thread that impressive pass through for Calafiori’s opener. The 19-year-old was also the quickest to react to David Raya parrying a shot into the six-yard box later in the first half.

Having Lewis-Skelly in midfield while Calafiori is at left-back adds another dimension that Arsenal did not always have last year, pairing buccaneering forward runs with exemplary vision.

Onlookers may be encouraged that the return of Declan Rice — who replaced Guimaraes — in the second half did not signal Arsenal sitting on their lead. They were still intent on taking the game to City and Odegaard showed exceptional poise and confidence to sit down Donnarumma before making it 3-0.

The Arsenal captain was sharp throughout Norway’s World Cup campaign, carried that into his pre-season performances, and continued in that vein throughout this victory.

The performances of Sunday’s starting midfielders may give Arteta more confidence to rest Rice, but the England international slotted back in nicely, making important interceptions at the base of midfield throughout the second half.

Art de Roche

This was exactly what Arteta and Arsenal needed after a truncated and slightly underwhelming post-World Cup pre-season.

Arteta’s regular starters have made staggered returns during the summer, which has contributed to some sub-par performances, but they set the tone in Cardiff.

The early goal may have calmed any nerves, but the team’s focus on staying in front was encouraging.

Gabriel, for instance, had some shaky moments in pre-season but began this match with a strong challenge on Jeremy Doku and did not let his standards drop. Alongside him, Cristhian Mosquera may also gain confidence considering the way he dealt with Haaland in William Saliba’s absence.

Tzolis impressed throughout pre-season, but playing this way against Manchester City is even more promising. He was decisive in dangerous positions, registering two assists, and was composed in deeper areas, a quality that helped Arsenal build the move for their second goal.

City still have players finding their rhythm, but Arsenal’s convincing win should be a confidence booster before Friday’s home game against Coventry.

Art de Roche

There is no two ways about it: that was really bad for City.

They were extremely brittle defensively and when they managed to create some chances in the first half, they were blunt in front of goal. They rarely played passes in behind the Arsenal defence, although they did get Doku into some dribbling positions and had a couple of sights at goal.

Anybody who came into the game with concerns about the build-up and the press, given some concerns in pre-season but largely due to Maresca’s work at Chelsea, will not come away from this with much encouragement. Ruben Dias and Donnarumma did not always look entirely certain on the ball, while the pressing — with wingers closing down Arsenal centre-backs — was exploited and the midfield were left exposed.

Arsenal are in a much more settled position, with a squad that has been together for a long time under a manager going into his eighth season.

The game was over when Arsenal scored their third goal in the 48th minute, and the substitutions made shortly after — Haaland and Nico O’Reilly went off after recently returning from their World Cup breaks — ensured that most of the second half was a painful meander to the full-time whistle.

A poor display but these are very early days.
